info.title: Metis API
info.description:
REST API of Metis Campus. Only metis-app's server calls it; the browser never does.

**Authentication.** Routes with a lock need `Authorization: Bearer <access token>` from Amazon Cognito (passwordless sign-in
in metis-app). `POST /api/auth/sync` takes the ID token instead and must be called once after every sign-in. Without a valid
token the response is `401` with no body. Routes under `/api/public` are anonymous: students enter with a share token or a
join code, and then use their submission's access key.

**Errors** are Problem Details (`application/problem+json`). A `400` caused by one input names it in `errors`
(`{ "errors": { "title": ["…"] } }`) so the client can show it next to that field. Some `403` and `409` carry a `code` the
client chooses its message with (`alreadyStarted`, `alreadySubmitted`, `submissionClosed`, `invitationAccepted`,
`invitationRevoked`, `invitationExpired`, `invitationEmailMismatch`). Messages are in English and are not meant for end users.

**Ownership.** A resource of another user answers `404`, never `403`, so ids cannot be probed. Organizations are the
exception: a member whose role does not allow an action gets `403`.

**Rate limits** answer `429` with Problem Details and, when the limiter knows it, `Retry-After` in seconds.

Ids are UUID v7. Dates are ISO 8601 and returned in UTC. JSON is camelCase; enums are strings.

post.summary: Proposes an assessment draft with AI from a topic and optional materials. Nothing is saved.
post.description: multipart/form-data: topic (required), level, instructions, itemCount (1-30), difficulty, allowedTypes (repeated), sourceText, files (up to 5, repeated). Returns an AssessmentDraft that can be sent as-is to POST /api/assessments; nothing is saved and files are never stored. 413 and 415 name the file in fileName and errors.files. 429 after AiGeneration:HourlyLimitPerUser generations in the last hour (default 10; every request counts). 502 when the AI provider fails or proposes no valid item.

400.description: A business rule or an input was rejected. When it is about one field, errors names it (camelCase) so the client shows it next to that input. A body that cannot be read (invalid JSON, not UTF-8) is also a 400.

413.description: Too large. fileName and errors.files name the file when there is one.

415.description: A file whose format cannot be read. fileName and errors.files name it.

post.summary: Starts the student's submission with their email (on the roster) and returns its access key; never returns the key of an existing one.

Returns the access key the other student routes use; it is never returned again. 400 for an invalid email (errors.email) or an assignment that is not open; 403 when the email is not on the roster; 404 for an unknown token; 409 with code alreadyStarted or alreadySubmitted when the student already has a submission, unless the instructor allowed continuing on another device (then the key is rotated and returned).

get.summary: The results of an assignment: averages, score distribution and per item achievement, answers, pending reviews and Metis helps.
get.description: Only submitted submissions count; those with essays pending review count with their provisional score (provisionalCount). Expired submissions are submitted first (lazy expiry). averageScore has 2 decimals and averagePercentage 1 (score of the submission's maximum); both are null with no submissions. distribution has five buckets of 20 points of percentage ([0,20), [20,40), [40,60), [60,80), [80,100]). Per item, in position order: answeredCount (responses saved before submitting), gradedCount, pendingReviewCount, averageScore and achievementPercentage over graded results only, metisHints and studentsHelpedByMetis. Also for an assignment of a workspace shared with the user (read-only).

get.summary: The instructor's home: reviews pending by assignment, open assignments and recent drafts, in one light response.
get.description: Only the user's own work. pendingReviews: assignments with submissions waiting for an essay review, most first (pendingReviewCount). openAssignments: open now, the soonest due first (no due date last), with closesSoon when due within 48 hours. Both carry rosterCount, inProgressCount, submittedCount and pendingReviewCount, counted without lazy expiry (a submission whose time ran out but nobody opened yet still counts as in progress). recentDrafts: the 5 drafts edited most recently.

post.description: { email }. Returns the token only this once (the link is <APP_URL>/invitacion/<token>, valid 7 days, single use, only for that email); there is no Location. Inviting an email with an open invitation reissues it, and the previous link stops working. The API also emails the link to that address: emailSent is true when the email went out, and false when email is not configured or the provider failed (the invitation exists either way, so the client shows the link to share by hand). 400 for an invalid email or the personal organization; 403 for teachers; 409 when the email belongs to a member.

post.description: { itemId, text } with 1 to 600 characters. Accepted under the same conditions as responses: 409 with code submissionClosed when the submission is no longer in progress, the deadline passed or the assignment was closed. 400 (errors.itemId) when the item is not part of the submission or Metis is off on it (metisAvailable false in the student view); 400 (errors.text) for an empty or too long text. Each hint rises one level (1 guiding questions, 2 a hint, 3 a partial example or ruling out one wrong option) up to the assignment's maximum; past it Metis gives no new hints but still answers. Returns question, reply (helpLevel null when it is not a hint), hintsUsed and hintsRemaining. Metis never confirms whether the student's answer is right. Without AI, when the provider fails, or past 60 AI replies in the submission, the rule-based version answers. Same rate limit as the other access key routes.
